hints: Think about when the heard pitch is lowest - it is when the source is moving directly away from the distant observer, so its speed along the line to the observer is greatest in the away direction.
Use the Doppler formula for a receding source with $f_s = 951\text{ Hz}$, $v = 330\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v_s = 12.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, then give the answer to three significant figures.
walkthrough:
**Picture the Doppler stretch**
Imagine you are far away to the right. The source whirls round at $12.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Most of the time only part of its velocity points toward or away from you. The lowest pitch you hear is at the instant it moves directly away from you, so successive wavefronts are laid down further apart.

**Apply the receding-source formula**
For a source moving away, the observed wavelength is stretched and the observed frequency is reduced:
$$f_o = f_s \times \frac{v}{v+v_s}$$
Here $f_s = 951\text{ Hz}$, $v = 330\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v_s = 12.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

**Calculate to three significant figures**
$$f_{min} = 951 \times \frac{330}{330+12.0}$$
$$f_{min} = 951 \times \frac{330}{342} \approx 918\text{ Hz}$$
This is the minimum frequency heard.
Final answer: $f_{min} = f_s \times v/(v+v_s) = 918\text{ Hz}$ to three significant figures.

hints: Think where maximum and minimum frequency occur - maximum when moving directly toward the distant observer and minimum when moving directly away, so sketch those two points on the circle.
Relate the distance along the circle between those two points to the period $T = 2\pi r / v$ with $r = 2.4\text{ m}$ and $v = 12.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
**Locate max and min on the circle**
For a very distant observer all sound rays are almost parallel. Maximum frequency is heard when the velocity points directly toward the observer. Minimum is heard when it points directly away. Those two instants are on opposite sides of the circle, exactly half a revolution apart.

**Find the period then halve it**
At constant speed $v$ round a circle of radius $r$:
$$T = \frac{\text{circumference}}{\text{speed}} = \frac{2\pi r}{v}$$
$$T = \frac{2\pi \times 2.4}{12.0} \approx 1.26\text{ s}$$
The shortest time from min to max is half of this:
$$t = \frac{T}{2} = \frac{\pi r}{v} \approx 0.628\text{ s}$$
Final answer: Half a period, $t = \pi r / v = 0.628\text{ s}$.
